title: feat: deduplicate generation requests
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Coordinates identical finite-generation cache misses through one Durable Object per shared cache identity; callers wait for and read the same completed R2 object.
- Covers non-streaming text/chat, embeddings, image, video, 3D, OpenAI images, image edits, and finite audio endpoints without provider-specific job IDs or generation deadlines.
- Authorizes every caller independently; only the detached generation performs billing and community rewards, independently of cache-write success.
- Keeps failure handling simple: no 202, unknown state, tombstones, deployment reconciliation, or direct-generation fallback.
- Preserves request IDs, balance attribution, fallback telemetry, multipart replay, and provider error responses across detached execution.
- Verified with Biome, TypeScript, the full gen suite (90 files; 910 passed, 6 skipped), and a live staging matrix including disconnect/rejoin, cache replay, and exactly-once billing.

Stacked on #13269.

gist.headline: One bloom, many visitors
gist.blurb: When several people ask for the same finite generation at once, the hive now grows it once and shares the finished fruit. Less duplicate buzzing, one tidy result.
gist.summary: Added Durable Object coordination for identical finite-generation cache misses, so non-streaming text/chat, embeddings, images, video, 3D, OpenAI image routes, image edits, and finite audio requests can wait for one completed shared R2 result with exactly-once billing.
gist.impact: Users making the same request concurrently receive the same completed generation while preserving independent authorization, request IDs, provider errors, fallback telemetry, and balance attribution.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy shared-generation garden: several small request seedlings with identical labels lead into one flowering code-plant, whose ripe pixel-fruit is distributed through neat paths to waiting terminals. Polli, wearing a tiny gardener tool belt, observes the orderly sharing while a cheerful CRT robot helps pass identical finished result boxes; the single bloom represents one detached generation and the paths represent callers reading the shared R2 cache object.
